text:
Rafael Mendes: 24h canary readout for KV compaction flag (hosted iad-1 + Dedicated pool ded-west-03). Overall looking good, but we’ve got one weird regression on a specific model/pool. Dropping numbers + proposal.

Rafael Mendes: Canary config (since yesterday ~same time):
- `kv_compaction.enabled=true`
- `kv_compaction.trigger.fragmentation_ratio=0.22`
- `kv_compaction.budget_ms_per_s=3.0`
- `kv_compaction.evict_mode=age_tier_fair`
- rollout: ~6% hosted traffic in iad-1 shared pool `h-iad-a10-02`, and ~10% of `ded-west-03` capacity

Rafael Mendes: Summary (24h):
- Hosted iad-1 (pool h-iad-a10-02): p99 decode latency down ~8–12% depending on route. Alloc-failure counter basically flatlined (was spiking during bursts).
- Dedicated ded-west-03: p99 improved ~6% on customer traffic mix. OOM events: 0 (baseline was 2/day).
- One regression: hosted sfo-1 pool `h-sfo-l40s-01` (still on canary slice via overflow routing) for model `llama-3.1-70b-instruct` route `/v1/chat/completions` — p99 up ~14% vs yesterday, p95 flat. Correlates w/ compaction “move” events.

Rafael Mendes: Dashboards:
- KV Cache Health (canary filter): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-cache-health?var=canary=true
- Tail latency compare (iad-1): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runtime-latency?var=region=iad-1
- sfo-1 regression slice: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runtime-latency?var=region=sfo-1&var=pool=h-sfo-l40s-01

Rina Kobayashi: Perf-canary gate is clean for iad-1 and ded-west-03. The sfo-1 slice isn’t part of the perf-canary job (it’s “real traffic only”), but I pulled the structured logs.

Rina Kobayashi: The p99 bump lines up w/ compaction bursts where we spend ~6–9ms GPU time in a single second window doing moves (budget is 3ms/s but we’re seeing catch-up behavior after allocation failure fallback). It’s not a constant tax; it’s spiky.

Rina Kobayashi: Example log snippet from sfo-1 (sanitized):
```
kv_compaction_event: {
  region: "sfo-1",
  pool: "h-sfo-l40s-01",
  model: "llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  reason: "alloc_failure_fallback",
  bytes_moved: 402653184,
  moved_blocks: 6144,
  gpu_copy_ms: 7.8,
  stream_sync_ms: 1.2,
  frag_ratio_before: 0.31,
  frag_ratio_after: 0.18
}
```

Marcus Reed: That matches what we saw in the bursty-mix benchmark pre-tuning: when alloc-failure kicks, it can blow through the “steady-state” budget to recover, which is good for staying alive but bad for p99 if it happens in a hot pool.

Marcus Reed: Question: is sfo-1 getting a weird mix of long-context + burst? The model route there tends to be “power users” with 16k+ contexts.

Omar El-Sayed: yep. sfo-1 has a higher share of long-context chat + tool calls (prefix cache reuse is lower -> more churn). When reuse is low, eviction pressure stays high, we hit fallback more often, and fallback compaction does a bigger move batch.

Omar El-Sayed: The allocator fallback path is currently: allocation fails -> do an aggressive compaction pass (bounded by “bytes-to-free” target, not time) -> retry. That’s what’s showing up.

Allison Grant: From an alerting perspective, this is exactly the pattern we said we want to avoid during canary: p95 stable, p99 worse. We should treat this as “needs tuning” before we widen.

Allison Grant: Proposed canary guardrail tweak if we keep it on:
- page if `p99_decode` delta > +10% for 15m on any (region,pool,model)
- page if `kv_alloc_failure_rate` > 1e-4 for 10m (because then we’ll trigger fallback and p99 will get noisy)

Sean Gallagher: +1. We shouldn’t roll back globally given iad-1 + dedicated wins, but we should stop the sfo-1 pain.

Sean Gallagher: Options I see:
1) Reduce budget + raise frag trigger specifically for sfo-1 to avoid move bursts during hot seconds
2) Disable compaction for that pool only until Omar can land a safer fallback (time-bounded)
3) Exclude only `llama-3.1-70b-instruct` in sfo-1 via runtime routing config (hacky)

Benji Okafor: We can do pool-scoped override cleanly via runtime config service. Something like:
- default canary: enabled
- override: `region=sfo-1,pool=h-sfo-l40s-01 -> kv_compaction.enabled=false`
This is a no-redeploy change. Propagation <2 min.

Rafael Mendes: I’d prefer (1) first if we think it’ll help quickly (less disruptive), but I’m worried alloc-failure fallback will still fire and then we’re back to burst moves.

Omar El-Sayed: Tuning knobs that should help *today* without code changes:
- raise `trigger.fragmentation_ratio` for sfo-1 from 0.22 -> 0.28 (fewer compactions)
- lower steady budget from 3ms/s -> 1.5ms/s (less background work)
But you’re right: alloc-failure fallback ignores those budgets. If alloc failures continue, p99 will still spike.

Omar El-Sayed: The real fix is to make fallback also time-bounded and allow admission control to kick in earlier (scheduler pressure) instead of “do huge move pass”. That’s in progress but not in prod yet.

Sean Gallagher: Given that, I vote we disable compaction on `h-sfo-l40s-01` for now, keep it on in iad-1 + ded-west-03, and open an action item to patch fallback behavior.

Allison Grant: Agree. We can message this as “canary continues; sfo-1 excluded due to tail regression; tuning in progress”.

Rina Kobayashi: +1. The wins in iad-1 are real (allocator failure basically disappeared), and dedicated looks great.

Rafael Mendes: OK. Proposed immediate change:
- pool override: `sfo-1 / h-sfo-l40s-01 -> kv_compaction.enabled=false` (leave eviction v1 as-is)
- keep current config for iad-1 + ded-west-03
- monitor 1h after change; if sfo-1 p99 returns to baseline, we proceed with 25% stage *only* for iad-1 + dedicated (no sfo pools)

Redwood Incident Bot: :information_source: Change request created by @rafael.mendes
- Service: runtime-config
- Scope: region=sfo-1 pool=h-sfo-l40s-01
- Diff: kv_compaction.enabled true -> false
- Tracking: CHG-21984

Benji Okafor: I can apply CHG-21984 now. Any objections?

Sean Gallagher: go for it.

Allison Grant: approved. please note in #eng-oncall handoff too.

Benji Okafor: Applied. Propagating.

Rafael Mendes: Watching graphs now.

Rafael Mendes: 35m post-change: sfo-1 p99 is back within ~1–2% of yesterday baseline, and compaction events are gone (expected). Looks like that was it.

Omar El-Sayed: Great. I’ll add a ticket to time-bound the alloc-failure fallback and plumb scheduler “pressure” so we can avoid the cliff. (We should also consider a model-specific cap for long-context heavy pools.)

Sean Gallagher: Action items before we expand canary:
- Omar: patch fallback behavior (time-bounded + respect budget) + get it behind flag
- Rafael/Allison: update canary success criteria to include “no (pool,model) p99 regressions >10%”
- Rina/Marcus: add a perf-canary scenario that mimics the sfo mix (long-context + low prefix reuse) so we catch this in CI

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: I’ll post a short summary in #eng-sre and update the canary checklist doc with the sfo exclusion + rationale.
